title: Data layer is disconnected from App rendering; production wiring is a stub
description: main.tsx wires `fetchPoolStats` as an inline arrow that returns a hard-coded zeroed `PoolCardData` for every descriptor. Nothing in the production path calls `runDataLayer`, `fetchFills`, `aggregateFills`, or `computeMarketStats`. The lines `void loadManifest; void RPC_URL;` are dead-code suppression for imports the wiring never uses. The whole compute/IO stack the cycle was supposed to ship — manifest loader, dataLayer, fillFetcher, fillAggregator, marketStats — exists only to satisfy unit tests and is never composed into the running app.
impact: AC1.1-AC1.5 are satisfied only against test fixtures; the dev server boot will render N empty cards (every stat shows the SENTINEL placeholder) regardless of sandbox state. The architecture diagram in spec.md (`page enumerates pools → reads each pool's inner state via sui_getObject → queries fills via suix_queryEvents → renders`) is not realised. A reader walking the codebase has to discover that no module composes the layers, which is the worst kind of design rot — modular pieces that don't form a system.
recommendation: Compose a real `fetchPoolStats` in main.tsx (or a new `src/composeDataLayer.ts`) that, per descriptor, calls the dataLayer/fillFetcher to get raw inner state + fill events, then runs computeMarketStats + aggregateFills, then maps to PoolCardData. Drop the `void loadManifest; void RPC_URL;` lines once the imports are actually used.
evidence:
fetchPoolStats: async (descriptor): Promise<PoolCardData> => ({
    poolId: descriptor.poolId,
    symbol: descriptor.symbol,
    volume24h: 0,
    lastPrice: undefined,
    midPrice: undefined,
    spread: undefined,
    depthWithinOnePercent: 0,
    sparkline: [],
  }),

title: runDataLayer returns void; RPC results are issued and discarded
description: `runDataLayer` is shaped to satisfy T-014's network-shape lockdown only: it issues `sui_getObject` and `suix_queryEvents` calls per pool, but returns `Promise<void>` and never surfaces the parsed inner state, fill events, or anything else upstream. There is no decoded shape, no handoff to compute, no result. The function name promises a data layer; the body is a fetch-tracer.
impact: The data layer cannot be reused by App or by any consumer that needs actual chain data. T-014 passes for the wrong reason: it confirms that calls happen in isolation, not that the data layer feeds the rest of the app. Any future test that asserts `runDataLayer` returns useful data has nothing to attach to.
recommendation: Change the signature to `Promise<{ poolId: string; innerState: PoolInnerState; fills: RawFillEvent[] }[]>` (or a richer per-pool record) and return parsed results. Have the App's `fetchPoolStats` call into it. Move the response-shape parsing into `dataLayer.ts` (or a sibling `parsers.ts`) so the chain-shape coupling lives in one place.
evidence:

title: types.ts is a stub; chain-shape-derived types are duplicated across modules
description: types.ts declares `PoolDescriptor`, `ManifestPoolEntry`, `DeploymentManifest`, `LoadedManifest` — but no module in src/ imports from it. manifest.ts re-declares `PoolDescriptor` and `LoadedManifest` locally; dataLayer.ts re-declares `RunDataLayerArgs.manifest` inline; main.tsx re-inlines the same parsed-manifest shape; PoolCard.tsx re-declares `SparklinePoint` and `PoolCardData`; fillAggregator.ts re-declares `SparklinePoint`; marketStats.ts owns its own `Order`/`Book`/`PoolInnerState`/`MarketStats`; fillFetcher.ts owns its own `RawFillEvent` (different name and shape from `fillAggregator.FillRecord`). The contract states 'TypeScript types in src/ are derived from that file'; in practice, types.ts is an empty shrine that satisfies the doc-comment test (T-022) and nothing else.
impact: The chain-shape file is the single source of truth in name only. Any drift in the manifest format requires editing four to five files (manifest.ts, dataLayer.ts, main.tsx, App.tsx via AppDeps, types.ts) and there is nothing that fails at compile-time when one is missed. The same issue applies to the order/fill types: `fillFetcher.RawFillEvent` is structurally identical to `fillAggregator.FillRecord` but cannot be assigned across without the consumer knowing both shapes happen to align.
recommendation: Move every chain-shape-derived type to types.ts (PoolInnerState, Book, Order, FillRecord/RawFillEvent unified, SparklinePoint, PoolCardData, DeploymentManifest, LoadedManifest, PoolDescriptor) and have all modules import from there. Drop the local copies. Keep the doc-comment in types.ts pointing at chain-shape.md.

title: manifest.ts uses node:fs and cannot run in a browser; main.tsx forks the loader
description: manifest.ts imports `promises as fs` from `node:fs` and uses `fs.readFile`. This module cannot run in a Vite browser bundle. main.tsx silently sidesteps this by re-implementing the manifest loader inline as a `fetch('/localnet.json')` and never invokes the `loadManifest` it imports (the `void loadManifest` line acknowledges this). The result: two parallel manifest-parsing implementations with no shared validation logic. The unit-tested loader (manifest.ts) is server-side; the production loader (main.tsx) is browser-side and untested. Drift between them is invisible.
impact: Validation rules differ — main.tsx's inline loader does not error when `packages.deepbook.packageId` is missing (it falls back to empty string), while manifest.ts throws. Users will see different error messages depending on which path runs. The cycle's 'manifest loader' tests (T-001..T-004) cover only the unused server-side path.
recommendation: Split into `manifestParser.ts` (pure: takes a JSON string or already-parsed object, validates, returns LoadedManifest, throws on malformed input — fully isomorphic) and `manifestSource.ts` (per-environment: `loadFromFs(path)` for tests/Node, `loadFromFetch(url)` for the browser). Both call into `manifestParser.ts`. main.tsx and tests then share the same validation surface.

title: fillFetcher.QueryEventsFn invents a custom shape and is never wired to a real client
description: fillFetcher defines its own `QueryEventsFn = (args: { packageId, poolId, cursor }) => Promise<QueryEventsResponse>` with a `RawFillEvent` shape that has already been pre-extracted into `{ poolId, timestampMs, baseQuantity, price }`. This is neither the Sui RPC `suix_queryEvents` shape nor anything the dataLayer offers. dataLayer.ts does not import or call fetchFills. The unit test mocks the function with hand-crafted pages, so the fetcher 'works' in isolation but has no adapter into the live RPC envelope (`{ data, hasNextPage, nextCursor: { txDigest, eventSeq } }` over JSON-RPC).
impact: Even if R2-001 is fixed and main.tsx wants to call fetchFills, there is no glue layer translating the JSON-RPC response into RawFillEvent. The fetcher's pagination logic is wasted because the wiring effort to use it is non-trivial: a missing `decodeQueryEventsResponse(envelope) -> RawFillEvent[]` step. The 'pure-vs-effectful split' is muddled — fillFetcher is effectful (issues queryEvents calls) but its effect type is fictional.
recommendation: Either (a) collapse fillFetcher into dataLayer (one effectful module that owns all RPC + decoding + pagination), or (b) keep them separate but make `QueryEventsFn` accept the real `SuiJsonRpcClient.queryEvents` signature and have fillFetcher do the parsedJson → RawFillEvent decode itself. Option (a) is simpler for Slot 1's scope.

title: Order type omits price; price is decoded from order_id even though chain-shape.md says event-source is preferred
description: chain-shape.md states: 'Slot 1 prefers reading `price` directly off the corresponding `order_info::OrderPlaced` event when computing depth ladders, falling back to order_id high-bit decoding only if the event is unavailable.' marketStats.ts's `Order` interface has no `price` field and unconditionally calls `decodeAskPrice(o.order_id)` / `decodeBidPrice(o.order_id)`. The captured Order struct in chain-shape.md does not even contain a literal `price` field — price must be carried alongside via the OrderPlaced/OrderInfo event stream — but the design has made no provision for joining the two streams. The compute function therefore commits to the documented fallback path as if it were the primary path.
impact: When the order_id encoding shifts (e.g. DeepBook upgrades, or an order with no companion event exists in the book), the depth/mid/spread numbers will be silently wrong. The design loses the documented invariant that the event-derived price is canonical. There is also a subtle naming friction: tests/marketStats.test.ts builds fixture order_ids using the bit-encoding (lines from red.log mention `ASK_BIT_OFFSET = 1n << 127n` in the test), so the test confirms the fallback path round-trips, not that the system can integrate event-derived prices.
recommendation: Add a `price?: number` field to `Order` (sourced from the OrderPlaced event in the data layer). Update computeMarketStats to prefer `o.price` when present and only call `decodePrice(order_id)` as a documented fallback. Keep the existing tests but add a fixture row where `price` is supplied directly, asserting it is used over the bit-decoded value.

title: PoolCardData widens depthWithinOnePercent and volume24h to undefined while MarketStats keeps them required
description: PoolCardData declares `volume24h: number | undefined` and `depthWithinOnePercent: number | undefined`, but the upstream producer marketStats.MarketStats has `depthWithinOnePercent: number` (always defined, defaulting to 0) and the producer fillAggregator.FillAggregate has `volume24h: number` (also always defined). The card therefore handles a sentinel that the data layer cannot emit. Conversely, midPrice/spread/lastPrice are correctly typed as `number | undefined` on both sides — the inconsistency is just on the two always-defined fields.
impact: Type signatures lie about the contract. Maintenance noise: the formatter `fmt(value)` runs an `undefined` branch that is dead for these two fields. Less harmful than R2-001..R2-006, but it points at the same root cause — types were authored per-module without cross-module review.
recommendation: Tighten PoolCardData: `volume24h: number; depthWithinOnePercent: number;` to match the producer types. If a 'no data yet' state is desired, model it at the card level (e.g. the entire `data: PoolCardData | undefined` prop) rather than per-field. Once R2-003 is addressed and types live in types.ts, this kind of drift is structurally prevented.

title: App.tsx fires N parallel fetchPoolStats with no error isolation between pools
description: App uses `Promise.all(manifest.pools.map(p => deps.fetchPoolStats(p)))`. Any single pool's failure rejects the whole batch and flips state to `error`, hiding every other pool's data. The contract says the page should render one card per sandbox-published pool; partial-success is the realistic case (BigVector slice churn from chain-shape.md mentions sub-second deletion + recreation that races sui_getObject). The design conflates 'manifest unreachable' (page-level error) with 'one pool's RPC blipped' (card-level degradation).
impact: On a normal sandbox with 2 pools, a transient RPC error on one pool wipes the whole UI and surfaces a generic 'Could not load market data' banner — the user cannot tell which pool failed and the other pool's data they could have shown is gone. AC1.3 ('one card per pool') is violated under partial failure.
recommendation: Use `Promise.allSettled`. Per-pool: if rejected, render a PoolCard with a per-card error sentinel (or a degraded PoolCardData with all undefined values + an error message field). Reserve top-level `state.status === 'error'` for manifest-load failure only.

title: App has no periodic refresh; sparkline-freshness AC is not architecturally addressed
description: Contract section 'In scope' requires 'Periodic refresh of the fill stream so the sparkline reflects new fills within 30 s of them landing.' App.tsx's effect runs once on mount with no setInterval, no polling hook, no swr/react-query, no manual refresh trigger. The 30-second freshness behaviour is silently absent. Tests (T-015..T-020) do not exercise refresh, so the green log passes despite this gap.
impact: AC1.3 / AC1.5 freshness behaviour is not implemented. E-001 (the Phase-F E2E that verifies sparkline updates within 30 s of a fresh fill) will fail when run against a live sandbox. From a design standpoint, retrofitting refresh later means choosing a strategy (interval polling, SSE, WebSocket subscription) which affects the data-layer contract — better to commit to one now.
recommendation: Add a `setInterval`-based refresh in the App effect (or a custom `useChainPolling(intervalMs, fetcher)` hook) that re-runs `fetchPoolStats` every ~15-20 s. Because `fetchPoolStats` is per-descriptor, refresh can stay per-pool granular and reuse the Promise.allSettled fix from R2-008. Document the cadence in code comments tracing back to AC1.5 freshness.

title: rpcId module-level mutable counter couples test and prod state across runs
description: `let rpcId = 0;` at module scope is mutated by `++rpcId` on every JSON-RPC call. The counter persists across runDataLayer invocations and across test files that import the module. JSON-RPC ids only need to be unique within a single connection / batch, so the cross-run sharing is inert today, but it is a small global-state hazard: any future test that asserts on the request id will be order-dependent on test execution.
impact: Negligible at runtime. Slightly harder to reason about than necessary; the module is no longer purely a function library. Flagged because the rest of the codebase consciously injects state via args (App takes `deps`, runDataLayer takes manifest+rpcUrl).
recommendation: Move the counter into a closure created per `runDataLayer` invocation, or just use `Date.now()` / `crypto.randomUUID()` for the id. Either way, drop the module-level mutable.
